mainTopic: The limits of the מדרס decree for קודש, and why vessels 'completed in purity' need טבילה but not הערב שמש, including whether that fits רבי אליעזר.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story: a sandal strap that was a מדרס fell into a barrel of holy wine and made it טמא. Because of this, חכמים ruled that someone carrying a מדרס may carry תרומה but not קודש. The גמרא asks why תרומה was not included too. It answers that this follows רבי חנניה בן עקביא, who limits a decree to the exact circumstances of the incident that caused it. To show his view, the גמרא brings a ברייתא and a story about carrying מי חטאת across the Jordan by boat. Next it asks how far the sandal decree reaches: a pure sandal, a closed barrel, and someone who broke the rule. On that last question, רבי אילא and רבי זירא disagree. The גמרא then turns to vessels 'completed in purity.' שמואל explains that a חבר finished them, but they need טבילה for קודש in case an עם הארץ's spit landed on them while still wet. Since the משנה requires טבילה without waiting for sunset, the גמרא argues it cannot follow רבי אליעזר. It proves this from the reed tube dispute and the idea of a public sign against the צדוקים. רב begins an answer for רבי אליעזר, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The sandal-strap story ends and the rule is set
steps.stepSummary: The end of a story: a sandal strap that was a מדרס fell into a barrel and made it טמא. Because of this, חכמים ruled that one carrying a מדרס may carry תרומה but not קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: His sandal strap broke. He picked it up and put it on the mouth of the barrel. It fell into the open space of the barrel, and the barrel became impure. At that time חכמים said: someone carrying a מדרס may carry תרומה, but not קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that explains where the rule about carrying a מדרס with קודש came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strap was a מדרס, made impure by a זב stepping on it. When it fell into the barrel's airspace, it made the whole barrel טמא. This accident is the reason חכמים forbade carrying a מדרס together with קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: An item made impure because a זָב sat, lay, or stepped on it
The open space inside the barrel
The portion of produce given to a כֹּהֵן; it is holy, but on a lower level
Sacrificial food, which is on a higher level of holiness

phrases.english: and the strap of his sandal broke off,
and he picked it up and placed it on the mouth of the barrel,
and it fell into the airspace of the barrel, and it became impure.
At that time they said:
one who carries a מדרס
may carry תרומה,
but not קודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story that explains the reason for the משנה's rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule comes from an incident where a מדרס strap fell into a barrel of קודש and made it טמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One carrying a מדרס may carry תרומה but not קודש.

steps.title: Why not forbid תרומה too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the decree came from this accident, the same accident could happen with תרומה, so it should be forbidden as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, תרומה should be forbidden too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule: the reason given seems to apply just as much to תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A strap falling into a barrel would make תרומה טמא too. So if the accident is the reason, why did חכמים forbid only קודש?

phrases.english: If so,
תרומה too should be forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the scope of the rule set in step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The danger from the accident applies to תרומה as well, so the decree should cover it too.

steps.title: This follows רבי חנניה בן עקביא
steps.stepSummary: The rule follows רבי חנניה בן עקביא, who holds that a decree made because of an incident covers only the exact circumstances of that incident.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי חנניה בן עקביא, who said: they forbade it only in the Jordan, only in a boat, just like the incident that happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this rule follows a תנא who limits decrees to the exact case that caused them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי חנניה בן עקביא, when חכמים made a decree because of an incident, they did not stretch it to similar cases. The incident involved קודש, so the decree covers only קודש, not תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows one approach to how far a rabbinic decree reaches: only as far as the incident that caused it.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
It is רבי חנניה בן עקביא,
who said: they forbade only in the Jordan,
and in a boat, just like the incident that happened.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the rule to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A decree should cover every case with the same danger, including תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי חנניה בן עקביא, a decree covers only the exact situation of its incident, which involved קודש.

steps.title: The ברייתא on carrying מי חטאת across rivers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא behind רבי חנניה's statement: the תנא קמא lists many forbidden ways of moving מי חטאת and אפר חטאת across a river, permits a bridge, and applies this to all rivers.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it? As a ברייתא teaches: A person may not carry מי חטאת and אפר חטאת across the Jordan in a boat. He may not stand on one side and throw them to the other. He may not float them on the water. He may not ride across on an animal or on his friend, unless his feet touch the ground. But he may bring them across a bridge without worry. This applies both to the Jordan and to other rivers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי חנניה said this, and quotes a ברייתא. This step gives the first, anonymous opinion; רבי חנניה's view comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids many ways of crossing a river with the purification materials, not just a boat. He also applies this to every river, not only the Jordan. Only a bridge, or walking with feet on the ground, is allowed. This broad approach sets up the contrast with רבי חנניה.

keyTerms.meaning: The purification water mixed with the ashes of the פָּרָה אֲדֻמָּה
The ashes of the פָּרָה אֲדֻמָּה

phrases.english: What is it? As it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִשָּׂא אָדָם מֵי חַטָּאת וְאֵפֶר חַטָּאת
phrases.english: A person may not carry מי חטאת and אפר חטאת
and bring them across the Jordan in a boat,
nor may he stand on this side
and throw them to the other side,
nor may he float them across the water,
nor may he ride on an animal,
nor on his friend,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיוּ רַגְלָיו נוֹגְעוֹת בַּקַּרְקַע.
phrases.english: unless his feet are touching the ground.
But he may bring them across over a bridge
and need not worry;
this applies both to the Jordan and to other rivers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source where רבי חנניה's statement from step 3 appears.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא about moving purification materials across rivers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: many ways of crossing are forbidden, on all rivers; a bridge is allowed.

steps.title: רבי חנניה limits the decree
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבי חנניה בן עקביא rules that the decree covers only the Jordan, only a boat, exactly like the original incident.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניה בן עקביא says: they forbade it only in the Jordan, only in a boat, just like the incident that happened.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנניה בן עקביא disagrees with the תנא קמא and narrows the decree to the exact original case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא spread the decree to throwing, floating, riding, and every river. רבי חנניה keeps only the Jordan plus a boat, because that is what happened in the incident. This is the same reasoning that limited the מדרס rule to קודש.

phrases.english: רבי חנניה בן עקביא says:
they forbade only in the Jordan and in a boat,
just like the incident that happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second opinion in the ברייתא, arguing with the תנא קמא of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The decree applies only to the Jordan and a boat, like the original incident.

steps.title: What was the incident?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what incident רבי חנניה is referring to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the incident that happened?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next step by asking for the story behind the decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנניה's whole view rests on 'the incident that happened.' To know exactly what the decree covers, we need to know the details of that event.

phrases.english: What was the incident that happened?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to clarify the incident mentioned in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The details of the incident behind the decree.

steps.title: The boat on the Jordan and the piece of a corpse
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quoting רב: a man moved מי חטאת and אפר חטאת across the Jordan by boat, and a כזית of a dead body was found stuck in the boat's floor. So חכמים forbade carrying them across the Jordan in a boat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A man was bringing מי חטאת and אפר חטאת across the Jordan in a boat, and a כזית of a dead body was found stuck in the floor of the boat. At that time חכמים said: a person may not carry מי חטאת and אפר חטאת across the Jordan in a boat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by telling the story that caused the decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The piece of a corpse in the boat made the purification materials טמא. The event happened on the Jordan, in a boat, so רבי חנניה limits the decree to exactly that. In the same way, the sandal-strap incident involved קודש, so that decree covers only קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-sized piece of a dead body, enough to make things טָמֵא

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי חנניה בן עקביא, a decree reaches only as far as the incident that caused it. That is why the מדרס rule covers קודש but not תרומה.

phrases.english: As רב יהודה said that רב said:
There was an incident with one person

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה מַעֲבִיר מֵי חַטָּאת וְאֵפֶר חַטָּאת
phrases.english: who was bringing מי חטאת and אפר חטאת across
the Jordan, in a boat,
and an olive-bulk of a corpse was found
stuck in the floor of the boat.
At that time they said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִשָּׂא אָדָם מֵי חַטָּאת וְאֵפֶר חַטָּאת
phrases.english: A person may not carry מי חטאת and אפר חטאת
and bring them across the Jordan in a boat.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאָדָם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כזית of a corpse was found in a boat on the Jordan that was carrying purification materials, so the decree was made for that exact case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The decree matches its incident exactly, which explains why the מדרס rule is limited to קודש.

steps.title: Three questions about how far the sandal decree reaches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the decree against carrying a sandal together with holy food also covers a pure sandal and a closed barrel, and what happens if someone broke the decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: The decree covers an impure sandal, but what about a pure sandal? It covers an open barrel, but what about a closed barrel? And if someone broke the rule and carried them together, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises three questions about how far the sandal-and-barrel decree from step 1 goes: does it cover only cases like the original incident (an impure sandal, an open barrel), and what happens if someone broke it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original incident had an impure sandal and an open barrel. So the first two questions ask whether a pure sandal or a closed barrel is also included. The third question is different. It does not ask what is forbidden. It asks whether the holy food becomes impure if someone carried it anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked; an open question raised in the בית מדרש
An impure sandal (one made impure by a זב stepping on it)
An open barrel or a closed barrel
He broke the rule and carried them together anyway

phrases.english: They asked:
An impure sandal is included, but what about a pure sandal?
An open barrel is included, but what about a closed barrel?
If he broke the rule and carried, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the מדרס decree of step 1 and asks how far it reaches beyond the details of the original incident.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the decree cover a pure sandal or a closed barrel, and is the holy food impure if someone broke the decree?

steps.title: רבי אילא and רבי זירא disagree about someone who broke the decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילא says that if someone broke the decree and carried them together, the holy food is impure. רבי זירא says it stays pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא said: If he broke the rule and carried, it is impure. רבי זירא said: If he broke the rule and carried, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers only the third question, and two אמוראים disagree about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אילא holds that חכמים made the food impure when someone breaks their decree. רבי זירא holds that the decree only forbids carrying them together; once it has happened, the food stays pure. The first two questions are left without an answer.
steps.confusionAlert: Only the third question (עבר ונשא) is answered here. Don't think the questions about the pure sandal and the closed barrel were settled.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ila said:
If he broke the rule and carried, it is impure.
Rabbi Zeira said:
If he broke the rule and carried, it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אִילָא אָמַר: אִם עָבַר וְנָשָׂא — טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the third question from step 8, with two opposing opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אילא says the food is impure. רבי זירא says it stays pure.

steps.title: Who finished making the vessels 'completed in purity'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about vessels completed in purity and asks who finished making them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Vessels that were completed in purity' and so on. Who completed them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה. It asks who did the final work on these vessels, and this sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says these vessels need טבילה for קודש but not for תרומה. To understand why, we first need to know whose hands finished them. The question opens two possibilities, and the גמרא tests each one next.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels that were finished in a state of purity
And so on; the quote of the משנה continues

phrases.english: Vessels that were completed in purity, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which says these vessels need טבילה for קודש but not for תרומה.

phrases.english: Who completed them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was it a חבר or an עם הארץ who finished making the vessels?

steps.title: If a חבר finished them, why do they need immersion?
steps.stepSummary: If a careful חבר finished the vessels, they should be pure, so the משנה's requirement of טבילה seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say a חבר completed them, why do they need immersion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possibility and finds a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חבר is careful about the laws of purity. Vessels he finished should be completely pure, so why would the משנה require טבילה for קודש?

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introducing a possibility that will be challenged)
A person who is careful about the laws of purity

phrases.english: If you say a chaver completed them,
why do they need immersion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that a חבר finished the vessels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חבר's vessels are pure, so requiring טבילה makes no sense.

steps.title: If an עם הארץ finished them, how are they 'pure'?
steps.stepSummary: If an עם הארץ finished the vessels, his touch would make them impure, so the משנה could not call them 'completed in purity.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, an עם הארץ completed them. But would you call them 'completed in purity'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second possibility and finds a problem with that one too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vessels touched by an עם הארץ are treated as impure. Then the משנה's words 'completed in purity' would not fit. Both possibilities now seem to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is not careful about the laws of purity

phrases.english: Rather, an am ha'aretz completed them —
would you call them 'completed in purity'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the second possibility after the first one failed, and challenges it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that an עם הארץ finished the vessels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עם הארץ's touch makes things impure, so the משנה's wording 'in purity' would not fit.

steps.title: שמואל: a חבר finished them, but we worry about an עם הארץ's spit
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that a חבר did finish the vessels. They still need טבילה for קודש because an עם הארץ's spit may have landed on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said in the name of רב מתנה, in the name of שמואל: Really, a חבר completed them, and they need immersion because of the spit of an עם הארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל resolves the problem by going back to the first possibility. He gives a new reason for the טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vessels really were finished in purity, so the משנה's wording fits. But for קודש, which needs extra care, חכמים worried that an עם הארץ's spit (which is impure if he is a זב) may have landed on them. That is why טבילה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; in truth (going back to an earlier possibility)

steps.whatToRemember: The vessels were finished by a חבר, so they are 'completed in purity.' The טבילה for קודש is an extra stringency because of a possible drop of an עם הארץ's spit.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Sheila said
that Rav Mattana said that Shmuel said:
Really, a chaver completed them,
and it is because of the spittle of an am ha'aretz.
phrases.notes: צינורא means spit. The worry is that some of an עם הארץ's spit landed on the vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both challenges by going back to the חבר possibility with a new reason for the טבילה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Returns to the first possibility and gives a new reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חבר's vessels would need no טבילה at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חבר finished them, but for קודש we worry that an עם הארץ's spit landed on them.

steps.title: When could the spit have landed on the vessel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: before the vessel was finished it cannot become impure, and after it was finished the חבר guards it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When did the spit fall? If you say before he finished the vessel, it is not a vessel yet. But if after he finished it, he is careful with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's answer by asking exactly when the עם הארץ's spit could have fallen on the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that is not yet a finished vessel cannot become טמא at all. Once it is finished, the חבר watches it carefully. So neither moment seems to leave room for the spit to make it impure.

phrases.english: When did it (the spit) fall?
If you say before he finished it,
then it is not a vessel yet.
phrases.notes: An unfinished vessel cannot become impure, so spit landing then would not matter.

phrases.english: But if after he finished it,
he is surely careful with it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer from step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the worry is an עם הארץ's spit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Before completion the item cannot become impure, and after completion the חבר guards it, so there is no time when the spit could matter.

steps.title: The spit fell earlier and may still have been wet
steps.stepSummary: The spit landed before the vessel was finished, but it might still have been wet at the moment the vessel was completed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it fell before he finished it, and perhaps at the moment he finished it, the spit was still wet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the spit fell before the vessel was finished and may still have been wet when it was completed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wet spit can still make something impure. If it was still wet when the vessel became a finished vessel, it could make the vessel impure at that moment. The חבר may simply not have noticed it, so טבילה is needed.

phrases.english: Really, it fell before he finished it,
and perhaps at the moment he finished it
it (the spit) was still wet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the timing of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Spit that fell before completion cannot matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: Spit that fell before completion can still make the vessel impure if it was wet when the vessel was finished.
steps.whatToRemember: The concern is spit that landed before the vessel was finished and was still wet the moment it became a vessel.

steps.title: Only immersion is needed, not waiting for sunset
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's wording, the vessel needs טבילה but not הערב שמש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immersion, yes; the setting of the sun, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from the משנה's wording: the vessel needs only טבילה and does not have to wait for sunset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually something immersed is not fully pure until nightfall (הערב שמש). Since the משנה mentions only טבילה, these vessels are pure right after immersion. This prepares the next step, which asks whose view that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunset, the waiting period after immersion

phrases.english: Immersion, yes;
sunset, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new inference from the משנה quoted in step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessels completed in purity need טבילה for קודש but not הערב שמש.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר: the reed tube case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says our משנה is not like רבי אליעזר and cites the dispute about a reed tube cut for חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבי אליעזר, as we learned: a tube that one cut for חטאת: רבי אליעזר says he should immerse it right away; רבי יהושע says he should make it impure and afterward immerse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects our משנה to a dispute about a reed tube cut to hold the ashes of the red heifer, the פרה אדומה. It says our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the tube case, רבי אליעזר says to immerse the new tube right away. רבי יהושע says to first make it impure on purpose and then immerse it. The גמרא now looks at how that case was discussed, because it raises the same questions as ours.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the ashes of the פָּרָה אֲדֻמָּה

phrases.english: Our mishna is not like Rabbi Eliezer,
as we learned: a tube that one cut for the purification ashes,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in פרה 5:4.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: he should immerse it right away.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
he should make it impure and afterward immerse it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the inference of step 16 within a known dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר in the dispute about a tube cut for חטאת.

steps.title: Who cut the tube?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls the earlier discussion of the tube case, which began by asking who cut it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: who cut it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls how the tube משנה was discussed, starting with the question of who cut the tube. This sets up two challenges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question the גמרא asked about our vessels in step 10. It shows that the two cases have the same structure.

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
who cut it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of the tube case cited in step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a חבר or an עם הארץ cut the tube

steps.title: If a חבר cut it, why immerse?
steps.stepSummary: If a careful חבר cut the tube, it should already be pure and not need טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say a חבר cut it, why do I need immersion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first possibility: a חבר is careful about purity, so why should his tube need immersion?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע require immersion. If a חבר made the tube, that requirement seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: If you say a chaver cut it,
why do I need immersion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first answer to step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement of טבילה for the tube
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חבר keeps things pure, so immersion should be pointless.

steps.title: If an עם הארץ cut it, it is already impure
steps.stepSummary: If an עם הארץ cut the tube, it is already impure, so רבי יהושע's 'make it impure first' makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if an עם הארץ cut it, would רבי יהושע say about this 'make it impure and immerse'? It is already impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second possibility: an עם הארץ's handling already made the tube impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע says to make the tube impure before immersing it. That instruction would be meaningless if the tube were already impure. So the tube cannot have been cut by an עם הארץ.

phrases.english: But rather, if an am ha'aretz cut it,
would Rabbi Yehoshua say about this case
that he should make it impure and immerse it?
It is already impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second answer to step 18 after step 19 rejected the first
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's instruction to make the tube impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something already impure cannot be made impure, so the instruction would be meaningless.

steps.title: שמואל: a חבר cut it; the worry is spit
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that a חבר cut the tube, and immersion is needed because of a possible עם הארץ's spit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר שילא said in the name of רב מתנה in the name of שמואל: Really, a חבר cut it, and it is because of the spit of an עם הארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's answer from the tube case. It is the same answer he gave for our vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tube is pure enough for רבי יהושע to say 'make it impure first.' But it still needs immersion in case an עם הארץ's spit touched it. This shows the two cases work the same way.

phrases.english: And Rabba bar Sheila said
that Rav Mattana said that Shmuel said:
Really, a chaver cut it,
and it is because of the spit of an am ha'aretz.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the dilemma of steps 19 and 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing one side and adding a hidden concern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חבר's tube needs no immersion.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חבר cut it, but immersion guards against an עם הארץ's spit.

steps.title: When could spit have landed on the tube?
steps.stepSummary: The same timing challenge is raised for the tube.
steps.simpleTranslation: When did it fall? If before he cut it, it is not a vessel. But if after he cut it, he is careful with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same timing challenge about the tube as it asked about our vessels in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before it was cut, the reed was not a vessel and could not become impure. After it was cut, the חבר watched it carefully. So again there seems to be no time when the spit could matter.

phrases.english: When did it fall?
If you say before he cut it,
then it is not a vessel yet,
but if after he cut it,
he is surely careful with it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's spit explanation in the tube case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no time when the spit could make the tube impure.

steps.title: The spit fell before cutting and was still wet
steps.stepSummary: The spit fell before the tube was cut but might still have been wet when it was cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it fell before he cut it; perhaps at the moment he cut it, it was still wet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as in step 15: the spit landed earlier and might still have been wet when the tube became a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The moment the reed was cut, it became a vessel. If wet spit was on it then, it became impure. So both our vessels and the tube need immersion for the same reason.
steps.whatToRemember: In both cases, a חבר made the item, and immersion is needed because spit may have landed before it was finished and still been wet when it became a vessel.

phrases.english: Really, it fell before he cut it;
perhaps at the moment he cut it
it was still wet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the timing of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Spit that fell before the cutting cannot matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wet spit present at the moment of cutting makes the new vessel impure.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's view gives a sign against the צדוקים
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהושע, making the tube impure and then immersing it shows that we reject the צדוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבי יהושע, because his method creates a clear sign against the צדוקים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that רבי יהושע's ruling, make the tube impure and then immerse it, fits well because it creates a public sign against the צדוקים. This sets up a comparison with רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's odd ruling, making a pure tube impure on purpose and then immersing it, has a clear purpose. It creates a 'היכירא', a visible sign that we do not follow the צדוקים, who demanded full purity with sunset for the פרה אדומה. This is the first half of the proof that our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר (step 17).

keyTerms.meaning: It works well / granted (it sets up a contrast with a view that does not work as well)
A visible sign or public demonstration
The צדוקים, a group that rejected the Oral Torah of the חכמים

phrases.english: It is fine according to Rabbi Yehoshua,
that is how there is a recognizable sign against the Sadducees.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, הַיְינוּ דְּאִיכָּא הֶיכֵּירָא לְצַדּוּקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the timing of the spit to the reason behind רבי יהושע's 'make it impure first', and opens a comparison with רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע's 'make it impure, then immerse' serves as a public sign against the צדוקים.

steps.title: The משנה about making the כהן of the פרה impure
steps.stepSummary: A משנה proves that the חכמים made people impure on purpose for the פרה אדומה in order to reject the צדוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: they would make the כהן who burns the פרה impure, to reject the view of the צדוקים, who said it had to be done by people whose sun had already set.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה as the source for the idea of a 'sign against the צדוקים'. They made the כהן impure, then immersed him, and let him burn the פרה before sunset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקים held that anyone working on the פרה אדומה must wait for sunset after טבילה. The חכמים held that טבילה alone is enough for the פרה, and to prove it they made the כהן impure on purpose. רבי יהושע's tube follows the same pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: The פרה אדומה (red heifer), burned to make ashes for purification
Literally 'to take out of their heart': to reject their opinion
People whose sun has set: they immersed and then waited until nightfall

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
They would make the priest impure
who burns the red heifer,
to counter the opinion of the Sadducees,
who used to say:
It was done only by those whose sun had set.
phrases.notes: That is, people who immersed and then waited until nightfall to be fully pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מְטַמְּאִין הָיוּ אֶת הַכֹּהֵן הַשּׂוֹרֵף אֶת הַפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the 'sign against the צדוקים' idea mentioned in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים deliberately made people impure, then immersed them, to show they reject the צדוקים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in פרה (3:7) about making the כהן who burns the פרה impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains a strange practice, making something impure on purpose, as a deliberate halachic statement against the צדוקים.

steps.title: Where is the sign against the צדוקים for רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: For רבי אליעזר, there is a sign only if a vessel would normally need sunset. If it would not, his ruling shows nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רבי אליעזר: if normally we need sunset, then using the tube right after טבילה is a sign against the צדוקים. But if normally we do not need sunset, what sign against the צדוקים is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's view. He just immerses the tube, so it only counts as a sign against the צדוקים if normally sunset would be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign works by doing something the צדוקים reject: using an item before sunset. If ordinary vessels in this situation need sunset, skipping it for the tube is a real statement. But if ordinary vessels never need sunset here, immersing without sunset is just normal and proves nothing. That suggests רבי אליעזר must require sunset normally.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunset: waiting until nightfall after טבילה to become fully pure

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי אליעזר ignores the צדוקים. It is asking how his ruling could work as a sign, and that depends on whether sunset is normally required.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Eliezer,
granted, if you say
that generally we require sunset,
that is how there is a sign against the Sadducees.
phrases.notes: Because the tube would be used right after immersion, without the usual wait for sunset.

phrases.english: But if you say
that generally we do not require sunset,
what sign against the Sadducees is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּעָלְמָא בָּעֵינַן הֶעֱרֵב שֶׁמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 17: by the 'sign against the צדוקים' standard of steps 24-25, רבי אליעזר must normally require הערב שמש, so our משנה (step 16) does not follow him.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that our משנה (טבילה without הערב שמש) could follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sign against the צדוקים needs a departure from the normal need for sunset. If no sunset is normally needed, רבי אליעזר's ruling has no sign, so he must hold that sunset is normally required.

steps.title: רב begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: רב starts to answer how רבי אליעזר's view still has a sign against the צדוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces רב, who is about to answer the challenge for רבי אליעזר. This line only sets up the answer, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב will explain that even if רבי אליעזר does not normally require sunset, there is still a way his ruling shows a sign against the צדוקים. The details come next.

phrases.english: Rav said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to the challenge against רבי אליעזר raised in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pending: the content of רב's answer follows in the continuing text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's ruling would show no sign against the צדוקים unless sunset is normally required.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב will show that a sign exists even without assuming sunset is normally required.
